facts.text: Springfield was founded in 1793 as the county seat, named for the many natural springs that supplied early settlers.
The town is the birthplace of Abraham Lincoln’s grandfather, who settled nearby in 1782, linking Springfield to the president’s family roots.
The historic Lincoln Homestead State Park preserves the cabin of Abraham Lincoln’s ancestor and a pioneer grist mill, a key landmark in the town.
The Washington County Courthouse, built in 1816, showcases Federal‑style architecture and stands on Main Street as a centerpiece of Springfield’s historic core.
Located along the historic Wilderness Trace, Springfield sits about 15 miles east of Bardstown and 25 miles west of Danville, placing it in Kentucky’s Inner Bluegrass.
